items.title: Gucci's new 'Made in China' sneaker models break with Italian tradition
items.summary: Philippine business daily runs the wire story on Gucci's Drip sneaker (circa $980/EUR800) carrying 'Made in China' labels, the brand's first break from all-Italian footwear production. Covers Gucci's stated rationale (needed a Chinese supplier's specific technical expertise) and analyst warnings that the origin label creates tension with the premium pricing Gucci still charges. Still-live critical story continuing to surface in SEA business press a week after it broke, relevant to the region's price-conscious luxury consumers.

items.title: Gucci comes home — and lands in Manila (Cruise 2026 preview recap still circulating)
items.summary: Philippine lifestyle outlet's recap of Gucci's Cruise 2026 Manila preview (Michelin-starred dinner at Helm, Greenbelt 4 boutique showcase, hosted by regional GM Alessandro Belloli) continues to surface in Philippine search/social referral traffic into October as the Cruise 2026 pieces remain on sale in-store. Included as a representative example of how dated activation coverage keeps recirculating in SEA entertainment-style fashion press; flagged here as old (nearly a year) rather than treated as a fresh signal.

items.source: Weibo (Sina Fashion channel, cross-border SEA/China fandom overlap)
items.title: Weibo discussion: will China-made Gucci shoes drag prices down?
items.summary: Chinese-language social discussion (read across the SEA Chinese-diaspora fandom too) debating whether the Drip sneaker's Chinese manufacturing will translate into retail price cuts. Thread cites Gucci's own line that production location and pricing are unrelated, and notes the brand has already made 1-4% price adjustments across markets since May amid 12 straight quarters of sales decline. No visible like/repost/view counters were captured from the accessible page, so engagement fields are recorded as null rather than estimated.

items.title: Thai fan-media post on Billkin and PP Krit's Weibo International Entertainment Awards wins framed alongside their Gucci ambassador status
items.summary: Thai-language fan-media account post (in Thai) noting Billkin and PP Krit's wins at the Weibo International Entertainment Awards 2026 in Macau, framed as reinforcing their 'Asian influence' and tying back to their roles as Gucci brand ambassadors fresh off Milan's SS27 show. Represents continuing organic SEA fandom amplification of the Gucci-ambassador storyline into early October; no visible engagement counts captured from the accessible post, so fields recorded as null.

items.source: Carousell Philippines / Facebook Marketplace Manila (marketplace observation)
items.title: Continued high volume of preloved/reseller Gucci Marmont listings in Manila marketplaces
items.summary: Observation of Facebook Marketplace Manila and Carousell Philippines shows sustained heavy listing volume of secondhand and 'preloved authentic' Gucci Marmont and other handbag lines, alongside numerous authentication-focused reseller boutiques (Purse Maison, Freya Collective, The Bag Hub). Sustained high resale supply is a soft proxy for consumer turnover/destocking rather than new demand; no brand-side sell-through data exists to confirm the read, so this is recorded as a directional community signal only, consistent with the critical-angle (resale market chatter) brief.

items.title: Song Weilong's brand collaborations for 2026, from Gucci to Guerlain
items.summary: Tatler Asia (regional T2 title read across Singapore/HK/SEA affluent audience) profiles Gucci ambassador Song Weilong's portfolio of brand deals, including his role in Gucci's 'The Gathering' campaign and runway appearances alongside the brand's Thai and Chinese ambassador roster. Representative of ongoing regional lifestyle-press activation coverage; balanced against the critical sneaker/resale items above rather than treated as standalone positive proof point.
